_readme: Seat/subscription pricing for the vendors and coding tools in data/models.json, plus the cloud marketplaces enterprises actually buy through. Refreshed manually — see scripts/refresh-plans.md. Every price is read from the vendor's own pricing page (rendered in a real browser where the page is JS-only), or, when that page lists a tier without printing its number, from the vendor's help center / docs, or from the vendor's launch announcement as reported by the press — `billing` says which source tier (1 = vendor pricing page, 2 = vendor help center/docs/blog, 3 = launch announcement as reported by a major outlet). Where a page shows both terms, `price_usd_month` is the annual-billing monthly equivalent and `billing` states the monthly-billing figure. A null price means the plan has no public list price (contact sales) — never a guess; `billing` then says exactly what the vendor says and what a reputable report adds. Per-token API prices live in data/models.json, not here. Validated by scripts/validate-data.mjs.

plans.billing: custom — no list seat price. What OpenAI actually charges (read 2026-09-20): a CONTRACTED seat fee plus metered usage, under one of two published rate cards. Source tier 2, "Token-based billing for ChatGPT Enterprise": "Usage charges apply alongside any contracted seat fees... the number of assigned seats at the start of each billing month sets your baseline seat charge, even if assigned users haven't sent a message"; usage is metered in tokens and invoiced monthly in arrears. Token rate card (USD per 1M tokens): GPT-6 Astra $10.00 in / $1.00 cached / $50.00 out; GPT-5.6 Sol $4.00 / $0.40 / $20.00; GPT-5.6 Terra $2.00 / $0.20 / $12.00; GPT-5.6 Luna $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.20 (https://help.openai.com/articles/20001415). Older/other agreements use a CREDIT rate card instead: 10 credits per GPT-5.6 Sol chat message, 50 per Sol Pro or GPT-6 Pro message, 30 per agent-mode message, 50 per deep-research task, 5 per image, 1.25 per voice minute, and credits per 1M tokens for Work/Codex (https://help.openai.com/articles/11481834). OpenAI does not publish a dollar value per credit. The credit card also states: "On average, Codex costs approximately $100–$200 per developer per month." Contracts can carry a spend commitment across ChatGPT and the API. Nonprofits: up to 75% off Business or Enterprise.
plans.includes: Expanded context window, SCIM, EKM, role-based access, domain verification, custom data retention, data residency in ten regions, 24/7 priority support and SLAs, invoicing and volume discounts

plans.billing: contact sales — no list price. Token-based billing is NOT offered for Edu.

plans.billing: no seat plan and no subscription — you pay each model's own per-token list price plus OpenRouter's platform fee. Source tier 1 (vendor pricing page, read 2026-09-20): the platform fee is 5.5% on Standard (pay-as-you-go), 8% on Business (pay-as-you-go), N/A on Free, and "Fee discounts available" on Enterprise. Source tier 2 (vendor docs FAQ): "We pass through the pricing of the underlying model providers without any markup, so you pay the same rate as you would directly with the provider", with the fee charged when you purchase credits; crypto purchases carry their own fee. Bring-your-own-key: Standard and Business include $25,000/month of list-price inference with no BYOK fee and Enterprise includes $200,000/month, with a 5% fee on usage above the allowance. Free tier gives 25+ free models across 4 providers.

Matters here because many enterprises buy Anthropic, Meta, Mistral and Amazon models through Bedrock rather than direct.
plans.includes: Managed access to foundation models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral AI, AI21, Amazon and others, billed per token

plans.billing: per token at the model's list price; enterprise commitments negotiated. No seat or subscription fee. Matters here because enterprises buy Gemini and partner models through Vertex rather than the consumer plans.
plans.includes: Managed access to Gemini and partner models on Google Cloud, billed per token

plans.billing: per token at the model's list price; enterprise commitments negotiated. No seat or subscription fee. Catalogue includes OpenAI, DeepSeek, xAI Grok, Meta Llama and Mistral models. Matters here because Azure is how many regulated enterprises buy OpenAI.
